names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 13 mai, «Sfântul Cuvios Gavriil Ivirul».
Read out of saint.gr's line for 13 Μαΐου, «Όσιος Γαβριήλ ο Ίβηρας», with the rank word and the epithet left off.

Read out of the Ohrid Prologue's third heading for the Julian 13 May, „Преподобни Јован, Јевтимије Георгије и Гаврил Иверски.“ — Преподобни left off, which is the `venerable` this folder already carries in `types`, and **Иверски kept**, which is the epithet "the Iberian" the heading sets after all four names and which the entry's first sentence confirms belongs to all four. **His is the name the epithet stands immediately after**, so it is the one of the four where the reading needs least argument; it was read as distributing over all four for the reason given on his companions' forms. Measured: a bare «Гаврил» would have folded with nothing, so for him the kept epithet buys consistency with his three companions rather than a fold avoided. The icon is in the body and the book gives him no year.
Name page 451 is «Гавриил Святогорец, Иверский (Афонский), прп.»; the rank is stripped and the rest kept whole.

death.note: doxologia.ro: «Cuviosul Gavriil și-a încheiat viața lui în pace (1028) și pomenirea lui se prăznuiește odată cu ctitorii cuvioși iviri pe 13 Mai.» The page's own title dates him «sec. XI».

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 12 июля ст. ст. — «Прпп. Иоанна (998) (Груз.) и Гавриила (X) (Груз.) Святогорцев.»

attestations.note: The second Georgian of the day's fifth entry. Name page 451 is «Гавриил Святогорец, Иверский (Афонский), прп.» and the reading life6517 is the Gabriel of the Portaitissa: a hermit of Iveria near the Iviron house who was bidden by the Mother of God to walk on the sea and receive her icon, which is the man this folder keeps. ITS OWN PAGE PRINTS BOTH DAYS — «Дни памяти: 13 мая , 12 июля» — the first being the Julian day the folder's other three rows already stand on and the second the day page that listed him, so the two books agree and no day moved. THE CENTURY DISAGREES AND `dates` IS UNCHANGED: the line gives «(X)» where the folder holds 1028 off doxologia.ro. No hymn on the day page under his name.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 13 mai — «Sfântul Cuvios Gavriil Ivirul»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 13ης Μαΐου — «Όσιος Γαβριήλ ο Ίβηρας»

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 13 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same civil day the Romanian calendar already keeps him on, and it is plainly the same man: the Iberian ascetic who drew the Portaitissa out of the sea. **He is none of the corpus's other Gabriels**, which the namesweep flagged and which were read. **The Greek dates the finding exactly** — the Tuesday of Renewal Week, that is of Bright Week, in 829 — and places his cave above the boundary of the monasteries of Xeropotamou and Saint Panteleimon; the existing `dates` object is **not** touched and that year is recorded here and in the added paragraph instead. **The finding itself is a feast the schema cannot hold on that wording**, being reckoned from Pascha, and it is not recorded as one: the row holds only the fixed 13 May that saint.gr keeps him on. **It says where the icon is now**, in the church of the Dormition near Iviron and to its east, and that a devout Christian of Nicaea had committed it to the sea to save it from the fury of the iconoclasts. **It adds a relic**: a portion of his relic is at New Thebaid on the Holy Mountain. No person on the page has a folder, so nothing is linked. No hymn is printed.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 26.05.2026 (13. мај ст. ст.) — „Преподобни Јован, Јевтимије Георгије и Гаврил Иверски.“

attestations.note: The day's third entry, an enumerated company of four, so one row each. **NO DATE WAS TOUCHED AND NONE COULD BE**: this book dates John, Euthymius and George and **gives Gabriel no year at all**, so the 1028 this folder holds off doxologia's „Cuviosul Gavriil și-a încheiat viața lui în pace (1028)“ stands alone and unchanged. **New here**: that he was the one **counted worthy to receive the wonderworking icon of the Mother of God which came to the monastery over the sea** — the Portaitissa, which the entry does not name, and which is the whole of what this book says of him. **The icon is not a `related` row and not a folder**: an icon of the Mother of God is not a person, and BRIEF.md §3 says an icon is no folder. **`related_add` of the other three**: this folder carried **no `related` key at all**, and the heading enumerates it beside them while the entry makes the four of them one company of founders — so John, Euthymius and George are added here and this folder is added to each of theirs in the same file. **Four reciprocal relations written where one folder had none.** `types` untouched: Преподобни is the `venerable` the folder carries. **No `locations`**. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion.
